newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault cuts prices to regain market share.
newsitem.headline: Renault cuts prices to regain market share.

text.p: Carmaker Renault SA said on Wednesday that it would cut prices of some models in France by up to five percent to recapture lost market share.
Renault's share of the French car market has fallen to 26 percent in the first half of 1996 from 33 percent at the start of 1995.
It said it would simplify the price range, lower prices for some cars and provide more equipment and options on some models without charging extra on some models.

"The supplementary sales volumes generated by this ambitious new marketing policy will generate economies of scale to reinforce the cost-reduction programme announced in March," the company said in a statement.
It said the policy also aimed to reduce the gap between sticker prices and actual prices, which have been slashed in France by a fierce price war.
Beginning on October 1, prices for Clio, Megane, Laguna and Safrane models will be cut on average by between 3.5 and five percent, it said.

The policy, which will also apply to new models, follows decisions by the group to leave prices unchanged at the start of the 1997 model year and to introduce Clio and Safrane models priced lower than their predecessors.
